stories.title: Army to detonate toxic lead azide in Iowa; nearby residents urged to evacuate
new_facts: Federal officials issued evacuation and mitigation plans a day before the controlled detonation of nearly five tons of lead azide.
Detonation is on schedule for Wednesday morning; freezing cold worsens instability and the lead plume could travel up to 100 miles.
Army says detonation Wednesday morning is necessary to avoid a future spontaneous explosion of the unstable explosives.
The Army canceled a Georgia firm's contract to safely neutralize the explosives, opting for detonation instead.
A federal appeals court on Monday declined to block the Army from detonating the lead azide.
Detonation set for 9 a.m. local time Wednesday; officials call it the best and only option.
stories.line: The Army will detonate nearly 9,700 pounds of degraded lead azide in Iowa Wednesday and recommends nearby residents, especially children and pregnant women, evacuate.

stories.title: Nvidia shares drop 7% as Jensen Huang's comeback rally cools
new_facts: Nvidia shares fell 7% as the post-reinstatement rally cooled.
Shares fell 6% Tuesday after a precise 31.5% jump on Monday.
Huang is due to face a Washington grilling the same day as Nvidia's GTC product launches.
Trump allies argued Huang was too big to fail and a victim of deep state maneuvering, per Axios sources.
By Tuesday morning the stock had reportedly given up roughly half of Monday's surge, about 40 points.
A viral AI deepfake video of Huang and Alice Huang in Ibiza has nearly 6 million Instagram views.
Huang got a hero's welcome at Nvidia HQ on Monday; reported affairs include two employees.
stories.line: Nvidia's stock fell about 7% after CEO Jensen Huang's return rally faded, amid debate over the reinstatement and Trump's involvement.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russian ships in Libyan waters, raising fears of wider war
new_facts: Zelenskyy says two Russian vessels were targeted in Libyan waters, a new theatre for Ukrainian strikes.
An alert issued Tuesday warns businesses supporting Ukraine of heightened Russian sabotage risk, including arson and threats to staff.
Gavin Hall (Strathclyde) on record: both sides are prepared to operate outside the conflict zone.
Ukraine confirmed Saturday's strike on a Russian ship in the Gulf of Finland, amid other incidents across Europe.
Russian cargo ship Sparta II was hit by a Ukrainian drone in the Gulf of Finland and towed home.
stories.line: Ukraine says it struck Russian vessels off Libya, raising fears the Ukraine war is spreading into North Africa.

stories.title: Anthropic stock drops below $83 IPO price days after Nasdaq debut
new_facts: Anthropic shares fell below the $83 IPO price after debut, changing the state of play.
Options activity surged after the drop below $83, with large put buys, call buys and put sales showing a divided market.
Fall tied to a fading tech rally after Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO.
Stock opened at $111.50 on Nov. 19, has fallen steadily, is down 8% below $83; analysts largely positive.
Shares down 12%+ to ~$76; Dario and Daniela Amodei each sold 3.37M+ shares worth $280M+.
stories.line: Anthropic shares fell about 12% to roughly $76, below their $83 IPO price, days after the debut.

stories.title: Blanche declines to answer questions on DOJ probe involving Nvidia's Jensen Huang
new_facts: Attorney General dodged questions on Nvidia probe; lawmakers demand answers on Trump's involvement in Huang's reinstatement.
Claims Trump strong-armed the board to reinstate Huang; introduces 'spy sex scandal' allegations and Blanche's DOJ investigation claim.
Blanche called Nvidia a 'good corporate citizen' while sidestepping questions on DOJ's role in Huang's reinstatement.
Nvidia's $26 million in ties to Trump is drawing scrutiny; Blanche refused Tuesday to confirm a Huang probe.
Blanche said he 'certainly' would have told Trump if DOJ was investigating Huang for crimes before reinstatement.
stories.line: Acting AG Todd Blanche declined to answer questions about a DOJ investigation touching Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, amid scrutiny of Nvidia's Trump-linked spending.

Court unseals records of search of Rep. Ilhan Omar's home, scope reaching back to 1980
new_facts: Warrant application covers 46 years from 1980; records heavily redacted; no criminal charges listed.
Agents seized Omar's phone, computer and passport in Oct. 12 raid; probe concerns her immigration paperwork.
The unsealed filings run to more than 160 pages.
Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh approved the search and ruled Omar could assert congressional privilege protections at its outset.
stories.line: A federal judge unsealed warrant records from the FBI search of Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home, which reportedly sought evidence dating back to 1980.

stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologizes to staff for code of conduct violations
new_facts: Board reinstated Huang as CEO; Nvidia stock rose 31% Monday then fell 7% Tuesday; chair Harvey Jones statement; Huang apology.
Huang says he is in therapy and acknowledged violating Nvidia's code of conduct.
Apology came at the first all-hands since his return; Huang said he made "very serious personal mistakes".
stories.line: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees for violating the company's code of conduct, saying he made serious personal mistakes.
